newsitem.title: USA: Price Waterhouse considers acquisitions - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Price Waterhouse considers acquisitions - WSJ.

text.p: U.S. accounting and consulting firm Price Waterhouse is considering acquisitions or joint ventures as part of a strategy to double or triple revenues during the next four years, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted its chairman, James Schiro, as saying the firm was not in a hurry to make a deal this fiscal year.
Schiro said the firm would report a 13.5-percent rise in revenues for the year ended June 30. He also said he projected a "substantially higher" rise in the current fiscal year.
Price Waterhouse's revenues totalled $2.02 billion for fiscal 1996.
Revenues from consulting comprised 34 percent of the total from 31 percent the previous year.
Schiro said he foresaw the proportion increasing this fiscal year.
